assumptions: Exactly a finite group acting continuously on the given profinite T, with the pointwise freeness condition. T need not be finite or nonempty. E is an arbitrary equivariant sheaf over h_T.
quantifiers: Every such T and action, every equivariant E, and all profinite test objects, including the empty one.
domains: Orbit is the actual quotient by MulAction.orbitRel with its quotient topology. Profinite compactness and Hausdorffness follow from the finite group action; a clopen basis is constructed from actual quotient images. h_T and h_Orbit are the universe-lifted continuous-map sheaves on the prescribed finite jointly-surjective topology.
conclusions: The actual orbit quotient is profinite. The natural h_T -> h_Orbit is locally surjective and its exact kernel is local orbit equivalence, hence h_Orbit is isomorphic to the universal orbit sheaf, compatibly with q. Every free-action equivariant sheaf has trivial full-test stabilizers and is realized on this quotient.
representation: Local lifts use the actual profinite fibre product of a map U -> Orbit with T -> Orbit. Kernel equality is split into a finite closed cover by the possible group elements, with a Fin index so no large-index cover is assumed. On nonempty tests freeness is checked by evaluation at a point; on the empty test the actual empty covering family forces unique sections. Realizable is stated over the abstract universal quotient, explicitly identified with h_Orbit by quotientSheafIso and its q-compatibility.

assumptions: Exactly finite Gamma, finite Gamma-sets T and X, and the given equivariant projection. Stabilizers need not be trivial and fibres may be empty. No surjectivity of X -> T is assumed.
quantifiers: Every object and every equivariant map over T; every family of finite sets with actions of the representative stabilizers; all permutations of each fibre in the realizable case. Both directions of the realizability criterion.
domains: Representatives are chosen by Quotient.out for the actual orbit quotient. Fibres are the actual subtypes pi(x)=t with the restricted stabilizer action. The inverse is the actual disjoint union of balanced products Gamma x_{Gamma_t} Y_t, with relation (g h^-1,h y)~(g,y), left Gamma action and projection [g,y] |-> g t. Finite sets carry their discrete profinite topology when passed to representedRecord; continuity of every function/action on these finite discrete sets is automatic.
conclusions: The original object is recovered by the equivariant evaluation bijection from the induced fibres. Conversely every family produces a finite equivariant object, whose representative fibres recover the supplied sets equivariantly. All maps over T are in bijection with all stabilizer-equivariant fibre maps; the bijection preserves identity and composition. The represented sheaf is realizable iff all stabilizers act trivially on their representative fibres. Its equivariant automorphism group is the product of the full symmetric groups of those fibres, as a multiplicative equivalence.
representation: No freeness or nonempty-fibre hypothesis is borrowed from S1. Stabilizer conjugation proves the equivalence between representative-fibre triviality and every point stabilizer. The represented-record proof then evaluates arbitrary continuous sections pointwise to prove the full sheaf criterion, with constant point sections proving necessity. AutOver is the actual subgroup of permutations of X preserving pi and the Gamma action; automorphismGroupEquiv preserves its composition multiplication. All algebraic classifications are stronger for arbitrary sets, with explicit finite-family and finite-reconstruction instances covering the task. The quotient is the same h_Orbit identified in S1, whose construction does not require freeness.

assumptions: Only the common setting: an arbitrary small discrete Gamma acting on profinite T and an arbitrary equivariant sheaf. No finiteness, freeness or point-detection assumption. Arbitrary sheaf B -> Q.
quantifiers: Every test object, section and group element; all target sheaves in the quotient universal property; all equivariant objects, all realizations and all maps between them; every sheaf base change.
domains: The quotient is genuine sheafification of the actual pointwise orbit presheaf. The generic-site implementation is instantiated by ProfSite, identified with the exact finite jointly-surjective topology including empty covers. Values are universe-lifted to the larger sheaf universe. Fibre products are the actual sectionwise compatible pairs, not certificate structures.
conclusions: Hom(Q,Y) is naturally the invariant Hom(H,Y). Realizability is equivalent to full-test stabilizer triviality and to the canonical E -> H x_Q (E/Gamma) being an isomorphism. The slice over Q is equivalent to the full category of stable equivariant objects. All realizations are uniquely isomorphic after their identifications are specified; all equivariant morphisms descend uniquely. For arbitrary B -> Q the corresponding classification over B is constructed, and the actual fibre-product comparison and quotient comparison commute with base change and maps.
representation: No D is preselected in the criterion: D is constructed as E/Gamma. Local orbit equality and sheaf separation prove injectivity, while comparison local surjectivity holds without the stabilizer hypothesis. The category equivalence has genuine functors, unit and counit. Uniqueness is for equipped realizations and does not incorrectly claim the underlying object has no automorphisms. The unrestricted base-change classification is not claimed to reflect realizability; reflection is the extra S5 theorem.

assumptions: Only the proposed one-point stabilizer condition in the common setting. The counterexample uses the finite group C2 and base T equal to a point.
quantifiers: Every point section and both group elements satisfy the proposed test; an actual Cantor test section violates the necessary full-test condition.
domains: RealProbe is the actual sheaf S |-> C(S,R), and RealOrbit is its actual sheaf quotient by constant real translations. The negation involution descends to this quotient. The Cantor probe is N -> Bool with its profinite topology and a concrete continuous injective map into R.
conclusions: The one-point test is insufficient. The quotient has only one point section, so the involution is pointwise trivial; the Cantor section is not fixed, because local equality after a finite cover would force its image to be finite. The resulting equivariant sheaf over a point is therefore not realizable.
representation: The source uses a standard Cantor-space homeomorphic embedding into the real Cantor set rather than the reference decimal-series formula; continuity and injectivity are proved for the actual map. The proof uses the actual finite-cover local-orbit theorem and is not a mock sheaf with stipulated point/nonpoint behavior.

assumptions: Arbitrary sheaf B -> Q satisfying genuine local surjectivity, exactly the task premise; no global section or global lifting assumption.
quantifiers: Every equivariant object E and every full-test stabilizer section. Both directions of realizability iff its base change is realizable.
domains: basechange_record is the actual E x_Q B over H x_Q B. Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective for the sheaf map means each target section has lifts on its covering image sieve, equivalent here to a finite jointly-surjective cover. Its quotient base is canonically B by the proved pullback quotient isomorphism.
conclusions: Local-surjective base change reflects as well as preserves realizability. A fixed-base section is locally paired with a lift in B, pulled-back stabilizer triviality fixes each local pair, and the sheaf separation condition on E makes the original section fixed globally.
representation: The proof uses local lifts only on the covering image sieve and never chooses a global lift. S3 identifies the canonical quotient of H x_Q B with B, so the implemented pullback realizability is exactly realization on the task base B.

assumptions: Only nonemptiness and representability of B are assumed by the proposed test. The counterexample is finite: Gamma=C2, T=Bool with trivial action and X=PUnit+Bool.
quantifiers: Every section on every profinite test is checked for the pulled-back stabilizer condition; a specific point section disproves the original condition.
domains: The projection sends the fixed PUnit point to false and both swapped Bool points to true. B=h_PUnit maps to the false base point. All sheaves are actual continuous-map sheaves and all maps/actions are actual finite continuous functions.
conclusions: Nonempty representable base change does not reflect realizability. The original object is not realizable because its true fibre is swapped. The pullback to the false point is realizable. B is explicitly nonempty, and its map is proved not locally surjective. Together with S3-S5 this separates sufficient full-test/local-cover checks from insufficient point-only and noncovering-base checks.
representation: The proof derives injectivity of the quotient map for the actual trivial base action by local orbit equality and sheaf separation. Thus a pulled-back section must lie entirely in the fixed fibre; the proof does not assume it or replace the fibre product by a declared singleton.
